---
title: "Study Plan, 3-Axis Diagnostic Protocol & Mastery Gates"
subtitle: "How to Train Recognition Reflexes, Navigate the 6-Part Curriculum, and Self-Audit with Blind Checkpoints"
---

Because flow algorithms themselves are black-box library calls (`Dinic`, `MCMF`, `Blossom`), studying network flows requires a fundamentally different training protocol from algorithmic domains like string structures or polynomial algebra. Reading a solution that begins *"Construct a graph where we connect $S \to u$ with capacity $a_u + b_u \dots$"* teaches you almost nothing unless you learn **how the author knew to build a graph in the first place, and how those capacities were derived**.

---

## 1. The 3-Axis Recognition Diagnostic Protocol

Whenever you encounter a new competitive programming problem—especially one with **no graphs mentioned in the statement**—run through these three diagnostic axes before writing a single line of code:

### Axis 1: Scale & Complexity Regime ($N, M \implies \text{Target Paradigm}$)

| Input Constraint Regime | Viable Flow / Cut / Duality Paradigms |
| :--- | :--- |
| $N, M \le 50$ or Grid $H, W \le 30$ | Multi-state unary chains (`切糕模型`, $O(N K)$ vertices, `Ch 12`), Ishikawa convex penalties (`Ch 13`), dynamic scheduling MCMF (`Ch 20`), or 2D rank-slot MCMF (`AGC 031 E`, `Ch 20`). |
| $N \le 300 \text{–} 500,\; M \le 5\,000$ | Standard Max-Flow / Min-Cut (`Ch 01`–`Ch 04`), Project Selection (`Ch 09`), Pseudo-Boolean & Bipartite Flip Cuts (`Ch 10`–`Ch 11`), Fractional Dinkelbach + Min-Cut (`Ch 14`), Gomory–Hu Trees (`Ch 16`), MCMF & LP Duals (`Ch 17`–`Ch 21`), General Blossom (`Ch 22`), Isotonic Regression (`Ch 24`). |
| $N \le 3\,000 \text{–} 10\,000$ | Unit-capacity bipartite matching ($O(E\sqrt{V})$, `Ch 05`–`Ch 08`), incremental parametric flow rollback (`退流`, `CF 1427 G`, `Ch 13`), or DS-accelerated flow graphs (`线段树/主席树优化建图`, `Ch 22`). |
| $N, M \le 10^5 \text{–} 5 \times 10^5$ | **Direction B (Flow Elimination)**: Segment-tree Hall Marriage (`Ch 08`), Planar Dual Dijkstra (`Ch 15`), Min-Cut DP / $(\min,+)$ Tropical Matrix SegTree (`Ch 16`), or Simulated MCMF via Regret Heaps / `Slope Trick` (`Ch 23`). |

### Axis 2: Objective & Constraint Structure ($\text{Algebraic Signature} \implies \text{Compilation Family}$)

1. **"Conservation / Routing / Redistributing Quantities with Bounds"**:
   - Fixed supplies/demands, degree bounds, row/column sums $\implies$ **Standard Flow, Vertex/Time Splitting, or Lower-Bound Circulations (`Part I`, `Ch 01`–`Ch 04`)**.
2. **"Pairing / Independent Selection / Grid Coverage / Precedence Chains"**:
   - Pairwise conflicts on a parity-bipartite domain, grid lines, or DAG chains $\implies$ **Bipartite Matching, König MVC/MIS, DM Decomposition, or Dilworth (`Part II`, `Ch 05`–`Ch 08`)**.
3. **"Binary Choices $x_i \in \{0,1\}$ or Discrete Levels $h_i \in \{1..K\}$ with Pairwise Penalties"**:
   - Logical implications $x_u \implies x_v$, "all-same bonus", $|x_u - x_v|$, or $\max(0, h_u - h_v)$ $\implies$ **The Minimum Cut Compiler (`Part III`, `Ch 09`–`Ch 13`)**.
   - Check the **Submodularity Determinant** $A + D - (B + C)$:
     - If $A + D \le B + C$: compile directly (`Ch 10`).
     - If $A + D > B + C$ on a bipartite conflict graph: apply **Bipartite Variable Inversion** $\bar{x}_j = 1 - x_j$ (`Ch 11`, `AGC 038 F`).
4. **"Ratio Optimization, Planar Grids, or $N \le 2 \times 10^5$ Cut Recurrences"**:
   - Ratio $\frac{\sum w}{\sum c}$, planar separation, or all-pairs min-cut $\implies$ **Fractional Dinkelbach, Planar Dual Dijkstra, Min-Cut DP, or Gomory–Hu (`Part IV`, `Ch 14`–`Ch 16`)**.
5. **"Weighted Assignment, Convex Penalties $x^2$, Contiguous Interval Coverage, or Linear Inequalities"**:
   - Costs per unit of flow, $\sum \binom{d_i}{2}$, interval coverage $\ge D_i$, or dualizing shortest paths/MST $\implies$ **MCMF, Convex Edge Splitting, Equation Differencing, or LP Duality (`Part V`, `Ch 17`–`Ch 21`)**.
6. **"Range Edges, Non-Bipartite General Pairing, $N \le 2 \times 10^5$ Convex Matching, or Monotone $L_p$ Regression"**:
   - Range-to-range capacity, odd-cycle matching, online pairing with regret, or $y_u \le y_v$ regression $\implies$ **DS-Sparsified Graphs, Blossom, Simulated MCMF, or Isotonic Regression (`Part VI`, `Ch 22`–`Ch 24`)**.

### Axis 3: Mandatory Pre-Coding Sanity Check (`Failure Mode Inoculation`)

Before coding any flow model, verify:
- Are all edge capacities $\ge 0$? (Check `FM-11`, `FM-14`, `FM-15`.)
- Can a chain be cut more than once? (Check reverse $\infty$-arcs `FM-13`.)
- Is the underlying conflict graph actually bipartite? (Check `FM-07`, `FM-12`.)
- Are internal data-structure or implication arcs assigned capacity $+\infty$? (Check `FM-09`, `FM-23`.)

## 2. Recommended Study Tracks

### Track A: Complete Linear Mastery (All 24 Chapters + 6 Checkpoints)
Designed for Division 1 / ICPC World Finals / NOI competitors seeking 100% coverage of flow, cut, matching, and duality modelling. Work sequentially through **Parts I $\to$ VI**. At the end of each Part, attempt the **Part-End Blind Checkpoint (`CP-I`–`CP-VI`)** *without* opening Hint 1 first: writing down the algebraic intermediate model and identifying the chapter archetype from an untagged problem statement is the single highest-yield exercise in this book.

### Track B: The "Non-Graph to Cut/Flow" Fast Track (`AtCoder ARC/AGC` & `CF Div. 1` Focus)
If you already know basic max-flow, bipartite matching, and MCMF, and want to master the unintuitive **English-to-Cut and Algebraic Compilation** techniques (including all four user benchmark problems):
1. **[Ch 02 · Residual Anatomy & Incremental Rollback](chapters/ch02-residual-anatomy-cut-edges-rollback.qmd)** + **[Ch 04 · Lower Bounds & Hoffman](chapters/ch04-lower-bounds-circulations-matrix-rounding.qmd)**
2. **[Ch 06 · Grid/Parity Bipartitions & DM](chapters/ch06-grid-parity-dulmage-mendelsohn-games.qmd)** + **[Ch 07 · Row–Col Duality & Birkhoff–von Neumann](chapters/ch07-birkhoff-von-neumann-row-col-edge-coloring.qmd)** + **[Ch 08 · Dilworth & Hall Flow Elimination](chapters/ch08-poset-dilworth-hall-flow-elimination.qmd)**
3. **All of Part III (`Ch 09`–`Ch 13` + `CP-III`)**:
   - `Ch 09`: Project Selection & Dependency Pruning (`ARC 085 E`, `[NOI2009]`)
   - `Ch 10`: Pseudo-Boolean Cut Polynomials & Submodularity (`燃やす埋める`)
   - `Ch 11`: Bipartite Variable Inversion (`AGC 038 F — Two Permutations`)
   - `Ch 12`: Multi-State Unary Chains & Disjunctive OR Cuts (`ARC 107 F — Sum of Abs`, `ARC 142 E — Pairing Wizards`)
   - `Ch 13`: Ishikawa Convex Penalties & Coarea Level-Set Cuts (`CF 1427 G — One Billion Shades of Grey`)
4. **[Ch 19 · Consecutive Equation Differencing](chapters/ch19-k-interval-coverage-equation-difference-method.qmd)** + **[Ch 20 · Coordinate Ranks & Manhattan Hubs](chapters/ch20-cycle-covers-dynamic-scheduling-resource-reuse-hubs.qmd)** + **[Ch 21 · Explicit LP Duality & TU Matrices](chapters/ch21-lp-duality-totally-unimodular-matrices-polymatroids.qmd)**
5. **[Ch 23 · Simulated MCMF (`反悔贪心`)](chapters/ch23-simulated-mcmf-regret-greedy-heap-segtree.qmd)** + **[Ch 24 · $L_p$ Isotonic Regression (`保序回归`)](chapters/ch24-isotonic-regression-matroid-intersection-synthesis.qmd)**

## 3. Per-Part Mastery Gates

Do not advance to the next Part until you can pass the corresponding **Mastery Gate**:

| Part | Checkpoint File | Mastery Gate Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Part I** | **[CP-I (`#193`–`#200`)](checkpoints/cp01-part1-foundations.qmd)** | Classify feasible vs. essential cut edges in $O(M)$ via SCC condensation; formulate any lower-bound circulation (`LOJ #115`–`#117`) and extract a Hoffman violation certificate without looking up formulas. |
| **Part II** | **[CP-II (`#201`–`#208`)](checkpoints/cp02-part2-bipartite-matching-duality.qmd)** | Constructively recover MVC, MIS, and Maximum Antichains via alternating reachability; win impartial bipartite walk games via DM decomposition; eliminate Hall matching on intervals into a segment tree. |
| **Part III** | **[CP-III (`#209`–`#216`)](checkpoints/cp03-part3-mincut-compiler.qmd)** | Compile any submodular 2-variable table or bipartite supermodular table (`AGC 038 F`) into normal-form cut edges; build multi-state unary chains (`ARC 107 F`, `ARC 142 E`) with reverse $\infty$-arcs; apply the Discrete Coarea Formula (`CF 1427 G`). |
| **Part IV** | **[CP-IV (`#217`–`#224`)](checkpoints/cp04-part4-density-planar-mincut-dp-gh.qmd)** | Formulate Maximum Density Subgraph in $|V|$ vertices; dualize $s$-$t$ and $k$-terminal planar cuts into shortest paths + interval DP; eliminate max-flow via min-cut DP (`CF 724 E`); build a Gusfield Gomory–Hu tree in $N-1$ flows. |
| **Part V** | **[CP-V (`#225`–`#232`)](checkpoints/cp05-part5-mcmf-diff-equations-lp-duality.qmd)** | Eliminate negative cycles via initial saturation; split convex marginal costs; transform contiguous range inequalities into flow conservation via $\Delta_i = \text{Eq}_i - \text{Eq}_{i-1}$; dualize any primal LP into an MCMF network. |
| **Part VI** | **[CP-VI (`#233`–`#240`)](checkpoints/cp06-part6-ds-blossom-simulated-isotonic.qmd)** | Sparsify 1D/2D range edges via persistent/out-in segment trees; reduce degree-$\le 2$ general matching via 2-vertex bins (`CF 1089 B`); design 1-push and 2-push regret-heap transitions (`模拟费用流`); solve $L_p$ isotonic regression via parallel binary search + closure min-cut. |
